family_note: NO family-level keys, and the family is Wall H.84 while the section is 'Wall units H. 120' - the fourth file of this shape, after wall_h72, wall_h84 and wall_h96_microwave_niche.json. printed p.253 prints this position inside the H.120 section and dimensions its elevation 84. THE PRINTED DIMENSION OUTRANKS THE DECODED LETTER: PJ reads H.120 in code_grammar.wall_units and here it does not. Height and mounting come from wall_h84.json.
extraction_note: One position, one code. Its own file for the same reason PE0696, PG0696 and PF0696 have one: inside wall_h120.json it would have taken the family's 1200, which the page contradicts.

wall_microwave_niche.description: Wall unit with door - 1 rh or sx - 1 microwave oven niche - 2 shelves
wall_microwave_niche.notes: THE FOURTH MICROWAVE-NICHE UNIT, THE SECOND WITH A SIDE-HINGED DOOR, AND THE SECTION HEIGHT MINUS 360 FOR THE FOURTH TIME (1200 - 360 = 840). Still an observation and still deriving nothing: all four print their own elevation. TWO WORDINGS ARE THIS PAGE'S OWN AND ARE KEPT AS PRINTED. 'rh or sx' mixes English with the Italian sinistra - every other family prints 'rh or lh'. And the niche is '1 microwave oven niche' where PE0696, PG0696 and PF0696 all print '1 ADAPTABLE microwave oven niche'; the registry keeps the catalog's words and does not decide whether the missing adjective means anything. Not object_class appliance_front: the niche is an opening in a Cesar carcass, and the machine that goes in it is the client's and nobody's order line here.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front of an 840-tall box, hinged on a vertical edge. hinge_side per order. NO hinge_axis - this one is not top-hung. The niche is interior and is not drawn.
